language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

<page-num>ᠨᠢ ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ</page-num>
<margin>ni ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ</margin>
<margin>律師戒行經第六卷上三</margin>
ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠭᠤᠯᠬᠤᠢ ᠳᠤ᠄ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠴᠠᠭᠠᠵᠠ ᠶᠢ ᠡᠪᠳᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠤᠭᠤ ᠳᠤ ᠤᠨᠠᠭᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠪᠣᠯᠬᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠪᠡᠢ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠮᠡᠲᠦ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ ᠨᠢᠭᠡᠨ
ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠰ ᠦᠨ ᠦе ᠪᠦᠷᠢ ᠳᠦ ᠪᠤᠷᠤᠭᠤ ᠳᠤ ᠤᠨᠠᠭᠠᠬᠤ ᠄ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ
ᠦᠯᠡᠮᠵᠢ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠮөн ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠵᠠᠬᠢᠷᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ
ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠ ᠂ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠳᠦ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠳᠦ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠ ᠄ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠦᠳ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠴᠤ ᠂ ᠲᠡᠦᠨ ᠦ
ᠬᠣйin-a ᠮөн ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠠᠴᠢ ᠂ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠠᠴᠠ
ᠠᠶᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠴᠤ ᠂ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠦᠯᠡᠮᠵᠢ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ ᠂ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠠᠴᠠ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠂
ᠪᠢ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠨᠡᠬᠡᠷ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠂ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠦᠨᠡᠬᠡᠷ ᠠйiladqaqui ᠄ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ ᠦᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠦ
ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠴᠤ ᠂ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ ᠲᠦ ᠦᠭүүлᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠦᠳ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠ ᠄
ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠦᠯᠡᠮᠵᠢ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠂ ᠮөн ᠡᠨᠡ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠶᠢ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠴᠤ ᠂ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠦᠳ ᠢ ᠬᠤᠷᠢᠶᠠᠵᠤ ᠄ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠨ
ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠦᠯᠡᠮᠵᠢ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠦ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠄
ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠦᠳ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠰᠣᠨᠣᠰᠴᠤ ᠂ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ ᠦᠨ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠦ ᠵᠠᠬᠢᠷᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠦ ᠵᠠᠬᠢᠷᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠂
ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠂
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠂ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠠ ᠨөгöge ᠦᠢᠯᠡ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠂
ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠦᠳ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ ᠦᠭүүлᠡᠪᠡᠢ ᠂ ᠮөн
ᠦе ᠳᠦ ᠂ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠠ ᠨөгöge ᠶᠢ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠬᠤ ᠪᠤᠢ
ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠭᠰᠢ ᠪᠠᠨ ᠂ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠠ ᠨөгöge ᠳᠦ ᠦᠢᠯᠡᠳᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ
ᠪᠣᠯᠬᠤ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠ ᠳᠤ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠨᠦᠭᠦᠳ ᠲᠦ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠄
ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ ᠦᠳ ᠲᠦ ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠳᠤ ᠂
<vocab>ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠦᠯᠡᠮᠵᠢ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ, ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ, ᠭᠡᠯᠡᠩ, ᠠᠶᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠲᠡᠭᠢᠮᠯᠢᠭ, ᠵᠠᠷᠯᠢᠭ, 律師戒行經</vocab>

<margin><term>ni</term> <gloss>volume marker corresponding to the Chinese character 泥 or the Tibetan syllable ni</gloss>, sixty-three, upper <note>original: "ni ᠵᠢᠷᠭᠤᠭᠠ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ"</note></margin>
<margin>Sutra on the Precepts and Conduct of the Vinaya Master, Fascicle Six, Upper Part, Folio Three <note>original: "律師戒行經第六卷上三"</note></margin>
in causing <note>one</note> to hold to it: furthermore, it is said that one will have fallen into the offense of breaking the precept; furthermore, in this manner, at each and every stage of the actions, falling into an offense: it is the Victoriously Consummate, Supremely Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss>; furthermore, in having commanded, he was victorious; in having performed the action here, he was victorious: the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>fully ordained monks, Sanskrit bhikṣu</gloss> heard this from the Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss>, and after that, by the grace of having heard it as well, the <term>ayag-a tegimlig</term> <gloss>venerable monk, Sanskrit bhadanta or bhikṣu</gloss> heard it from the Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss>, and to the Victoriously Consummate, Supremely Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss>, made known what was heard from the Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> and what I myself truly heard, and furthermore truly reports what was heard: having heard of the deeds of the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss>, when one has heard what was spoken to the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss>, furthermore the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss> have heard it: the Victoriously Consummate, Supremely Victorious One <note>original: "ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠦᠯᠡᠮᠵᠢ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ", standard Mongolian translation of Bhagavān, the Blessed One</note>, furthermore having heard of this very matter, assembled the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss>: having heard of the matter before the Victoriously Consummate, Supremely Victorious One: having heard what the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss> reported, and the Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> having furthermore regulated the deeds of the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss>, having furthermore regulated the deeds,
furthermore, the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss> spoke to the Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> of having performed this and the other action; at that very time, saying that this and the other had been performed, furthermore, because this and the other had been performed, he issued a <term>jarlig</term> <gloss>royal or sacred decree, Buddha's pronouncement</gloss> to the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss>: when the Victorious <term>Burkhan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss> issued the <term>jarlig</term> <gloss>decree</gloss> to the <term>gelengs</term> <gloss>monks</gloss>,

<summary>This folio from a Classical Mongolian Buddhist canonical text (marked in the Chinese margin as the sixth fascicle of the Sutra on the Precepts and Conduct of the Vinaya Master) details monastic disciplinary procedures. It describes how transgressions of the precepts at each stage of an action are reported by the monks (gelengs) to the Buddha (Victorious Burkhan), who then convenes the assembly and issues authoritative decrees (jarlig) regulating monastic conduct.</summary>
